- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent price spikes — apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a “reversion bias” correction: shift forecast toward historical 18-day average if price deviates >2σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 7-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33 → +0.67), model often misreads trend — adjust forecast to reflect “sentiment momentum lag” by delaying peak predictions by 2–3 days.
